effHelpIntro: The efficiency score is built from four components. Each is rated from 0 to 100, then combined by weight. The data comes from the timesheet for the selected period.
effHelpAttendanceFormula: Worked days ÷ scheduled days × 100. Paid time off (vacation, company-paid leave) counts in both the numerator and the denominator, so it does not affect the score.
effHelpPunctualityFormula: 100 − frequency penalty − severity penalty. Frequency = late days ÷ days with badge events, up to 60 points. Severity = late minutes per day with badge events × 2, up to 40 points. Time-off days are excluded — you cannot be late on them.
effHelpWorkloadFormula: Worked minutes ÷ the period time norm × 100. The norm follows the employee's schedule and the production calendar: holidays and weekends are subtracted, short days reduce the norm.
effHelpTasksFormula: Tasks closed before the deadline ÷ (closed + overdue open) × 100. A task in progress whose deadline has not passed is not counted, and neither are drafts. A task with no deadline counts as closed on time.
effHelpTotal: Score = sum of (component score × its weight) ÷ sum of weights, rounded to one decimal.
effHelpRedistribute: If a component has no data — no tasks assigned, or no work schedule set — it drops out of the calculation and its weight is spread proportionally across the rest. Missing data never lowers the score.
effHelpBonus: Overtime adds a bonus: 1 point per percent above the norm, capped at 5. The bonus applies only when the time norm is met — staying late while working half the month is not overtime.
effHelpSources: Face recognition terminal events, the employee's work schedule and its history, time off and vacations, the production calendar, and tasks assigned to the employee. The period never starts before the hire date and ends today.
effHelpTolerance: Late arrivals and early leaves are measured against the tolerance windows set in the work schedule. When the window is zero, any minute past the shift start counts as late.
